Yorkshire's Best Villages and Pubs for Motorcyclists

Yorkshire is blessed with stunning villages and outstanding pubs — two things that make motorcycle touring genuinely pleasurable. Whether you're riding the Dales, the Moors, or the Yorkshire Wolds, there's always a stone-built village with a welcoming pub just around the corner. Here are our favourites.

The Yorkshire Dales

Hawes is the Dales' capital and the gateway to Buttertubs Pass. The town has a cobbled market, the Wensleydale Creamery (cheese tasting!), and several good pubs. The Green Dragon Inn serves proper Dales food with local ales. Parking is easy in the large market square.

Reeth in Swaledale is a beautiful village around a large green with views up the dale. The Dales Bike Centre nearby has a cafe, workshop, and camping specifically for motorcyclists. The Buck Hotel on the green serves excellent food.

Malham is a tiny village near the famous Malham Cove limestone amphitheatre. The Lister Arms is cosy and biker-friendly. The ride from Settle to Malham through the limestone landscape is beautiful.

The North York Moors

Helmsley is an elegant market town at the western edge of the Moors. The castle ruins dominate the square, and the town has excellent independent shops and restaurants. The Star Inn at Harome (2 miles away) is a Michelin-starred pub in a thatched building — worth the splurge for a special meal.

Goathland is the real-life Aidensfield from Heartbeat and Hogsmeade Station from Harry Potter. The village green with sheep wandering freely is quintessentially English. The Mallyan Spout Hotel serves good food with moorland views.

Yorkshire does pubs better than anywhere in England. Real ales, honest food, stone floors, and a warm welcome — every village seems to have at least one pub worth stopping at.

The Wolds and East Yorkshire

Stamford Bridge has historical significance (the 1066 battle site) and a pleasant waterside pub. Beverley is an elegant Georgian town with a magnificent minster and the White Horse Inn — a tiny, unspoilt pub that's barely changed in decades.

Must-Visit Yorkshire Pubs

  • Tan Hill Inn — Britain's highest pub at 528m, remote and atmospheric
  • The Birch Hall Inn, Goathland — Tiny, traditional, with beer served through a hatch
  • The Falcon, Arncliffe — Filming location for the original Emmerdale, beautiful Littondale setting
  • The Blue Lion, East Witton — Superb food in a Wensleydale village
  • The Wheatsheaf, Carperby — Dales pub where James Herriot reportedly proposed to his wife

Practical Tips

Most Yorkshire villages have free on-street parking suitable for motorcycles. Pub food is generally served 12-2pm and 6-9pm — arrive outside these windows and you may go hungry. Many Dales pubs close Monday and/or Tuesday lunchtimes. Yorkshire's real ales — from breweries like Theakston, Black Sheep, and Timothy Taylor — are world-class. faq.q: Which Yorkshire village is best for motorcyclists?
faq.a: Reeth in Swaledale is hard to beat thanks to the nearby Dales Bike Centre, which has a cafe, workshop and camping aimed specifically at motorcyclists. Hawes is the Dales' capital and gateway to Buttertubs Pass, with the Green Dragon Inn and the Wensleydale Creamery, and easy parking in the large market square.

faq.q: Which pubs should I not miss?
faq.a: The Tan Hill Inn is Britain's highest pub at 528 metres, remote and atmospheric. The tiny Birch Hall Inn at Goathland serves beer through a hatch, the Blue Lion at East Witton is superb for food, and the Falcon at Arncliffe was a filming location for the original Emmerdale. Yorkshire arguably does pubs better than anywhere in England.

faq.q: When is food served in Yorkshire pubs?
faq.a: Pub food is generally served between 12-2pm and 6-9pm, so arrive outside those windows and you may go hungry. Many Dales pubs also close on Monday or Tuesday lunchtimes, and popular pubs get busy at weekends, so it is worth booking for dinner, especially in summer.

faq.q: Is parking easy in Yorkshire villages?
faq.a: Most Yorkshire villages have free on-street parking suitable for motorcycles, and towns like Hawes and Helmsley have large market squares. Even where parking is tight, bikes can usually find a spot, making it easy to stop and explore between rides.

faq.q: Which areas of Yorkshire are best for touring?
faq.a: The Yorkshire Dales around Hawes, Reeth and Malham offer stone villages and classic pubs amid limestone scenery. The North York Moors around Helmsley and Goathland combine moorland riding with pretty villages, while the Wolds and East Yorkshire around Beverley and Stamford Bridge are quieter and often overlooked.
